Security in every area: never weaken the hooks or the sandbox. GitHub is read and written only with the configured host and token. Never write to, comment on, close, merge or rebuild another Forerunner's pull request, and never rewrite its marker, guide part or status comment. Money and the person's control: no budget, wrap-up line, monthly cap or plan-share cap is ever passed; reading GitHub costs no model money; each person's spend stays on their own ledger and never appears on GitHub (no costs, emails, chat or ids in the status issue); when the app says it waits, nothing moves; no session starts unless the person said so (or the hands-off setting, off by default, or the decided continuation of the person's own session). Model-facing prompts and tool definitions are code: change them in the repository and assert the exact text the model receives. Words the person sees follow design section 5: one sentence read at a glance, CHF only, names not ids, "you" only for the person looking, no markdown, no raw states, a sentence promises only what the app does (run C's words stop at "each keeps its own tasks").
